title: VSift time anchor v1
description: Time anchoring (0.3.0, ADR 0029): the time_anchor member of ingest and session status data, which says when the recording happened by the real-world clock and on what authority. It is present only when the session has an anchor; a session without one omits it, and every timestamped item then omits clock_time. An anchor ties one position of the timeline (media_time_us) to one clock reading from one source. The sources, in the order clock times are taken from them: operator (ingest --recorded-at, confidence exact), quicktime_creationdate (the recording app's own local-time tag, high) and container_creation_time (the container's UTC creation time, medium: many tools write the time they encoded or remuxed the file, and some devices the end of the recording). A file's modification time is never a source, and an online provider's upload date is not a recording time. consistency says whether the anchors agree: single (one anchor, or no two that name an instant), consistent (every two that name an instant agree within two seconds) or conflicting (two disagree; clock times still come from the first source, and a reader should say they are disputed). Only anchors that name an instant are compared: a local time whose zone is unknown (a clock face, or a statement without an offset) is never compared with another reading. Clocks on the screen (ADR 0029, stage 2, the clocks command) add three sources at other positions of the timeline: screen_clock_confirmed (a clock whose zone the user confirmed, ranked after quicktime_creationdate), then, after container_creation_time, screen_timestamp (a moving clock that states its zone) and screen_clock (a dated clock with no zone, local only). All three are medium. Anchors are compared at their own positions, with each screen anchor's precision_us added to the two seconds. segments lists the gaps a clock showed: a gap in state detected changes no clock time, and only a person accepts one. Later releases may add sources and consistency values; a reader treats an unknown value as a reason to check the anchors list.

source.description: The anchor every clock time of the session comes from: the first of anchors.

recording_start.description: The clock time of the start of the timeline (media time 0) by the selected anchor.

anchors.description: Every anchor, in the order clock times are taken from them.

media_time_us.description: The timeline position, in microseconds, whose clock reading this is: 0 for a statement or a tag, and where a clock was best read for a clock on the screen.

clock_id.description: The clock on the screen this anchor came from.

precision_us.description: How far a clock on the screen's reading can be from the truth, in microseconds.

segments.description: The timeline divided by gaps a clock on the screen showed, in order; absent when there is none. The first segment has only segment, from_us and to_us. A gap in state detected changes no clock time: adjusted_by_us is what accepted gaps add, and an item after a detected gap carries segment as a sign that its time may be off by jump_us. Only vsift clocks --accept-gap, on the user's word, accepts one.

clock_id.description: A clock on the screen, as the clocks command names it.

clock.description: One clock reading. utc is the exact instant, when the reading names one: RFC 3339 in UTC with six fraction digits and Z. local is what the local clock showed, when the source said so: the date and time with six fraction digits and no zone. utc_offset is the local clock's offset from UTC (+HH:MM or -HH:MM), present only when both are. utc without local: the instant is known, the local zone is not. local without utc: a local time whose zone is not known, which names no instant; matching it with UTC logs needs the zone from elsewhere.

clock_time.description: The clock_time member of a timestamped item: the real-world clock time of the item's position on the timeline, from the session's selected anchor (see time_anchor in ingest and session status for whether the anchors agree). at is a point's time (a frame, a candidate's representative frame, an audio clip's first decoded sample); start and end are a range's ends (a transcript segment, a candidate's span, an audio clip's planned range). Absent members do not apply to the item. clock_id names the clock on the screen the time came from, when one did. segment says which segment of the timeline the item lies in, when a gap divides it (see time_anchor.segments): after a detected gap the time may be off by that gap. The whole member is absent when the session has no anchor.
